question: Across independently sampled species with fixed individual-level replication, does flower-colour composition diverge more as geographic distance increases within species?

fresh_metadata_acquisition.query_scope: one worldwide query per frozen species taxon_id
fresh_metadata_acquisition.request_error_policy: record zero fresh rows for that species; never redraw
fresh_metadata_acquisition.raw_photo_selection: deterministic geographic maximin after local eligibility, prior-ID exclusion and observer cap; first point maximizes mean great-circle distance to all rows, then each next point maximizes minimum distance to selected points; ties use stable row hash

premeasurement_gate.full_species_definition: exactly 60 retained fresh raw photos after all frozen filters
premeasurement_gate.if_pass: authorize location-blind measurement of only the frozen retained H9 rows

measurement.localization: same frozen ROI-v4 implementation and weights used by the completed random photo-first atlas
measurement.colour: same fixed generic sRGB-to-CIELAB palette and soft flower-only fractions
measurement.worker_blinding: species, coordinates, observation/photo IDs, observer/date and ecological context unavailable to measurement worker

postmeasurement_gate.classifiable_definition: measurement status classified_four_state_morph with retained soft four-group composition

analysis.photo_selection: exactly 20 classifiable rows per species by ascending SHA-256 of fixed measurement_id plus analysis seed; colour values do not enter selection
analysis.species_statistic: Spearman rho between all 190 pairwise great-circle geographic distances and pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences of soft four-group photo colour compositions
analysis.global_statistic: equal-species mean rho because each species contributes exactly 20 photos and 190 pairs
analysis.null: within each species independently permute the 20 fixed photo colour vectors across the 20 fixed coordinates, recompute rho and equal-species mean
analysis.support: postmeasurement gate passes, observed mean rho > 0 and Monte Carlo p_upper < 0.05

claim_ceiling: A supported H9 would establish a general tendency for flower-colour composition to diverge with geographic separation within species under a fixed-n fresh public-photo design. It would not establish a shared global boundary, identify a climate driver, demonstrate adaptation or selection, or identify pigment or pollinator mechanisms.
